preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is an integer between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(N, int) and isinstance(K, int) and 1 <= K <= N <= 10**5 for N, K in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, N and K are integers satisfying 1 <= K <= N <= 10^5.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(S, str) and len(S) == N and all('a' <= c <= 'z' for c in S) for N, S in test_cases_strings)
preconditions.description: For each test case, S is a string of length N containing only lowercase Latin letters.
The sum of N over all test cases does not exceed 2*10^5.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line) == N and all('a' <= c <= 'z' for c in line) for line, N in zip(stdout_lines, [tc[0] for tc in test_cases]))
postconditions.description: Each output line is a string of length N containing only lowercase Latin letters.

postconditions.expression: all(sorted(line) == sorted(S) for line, S in zip(stdout_lines, [tc[1] for tc in test_cases_strings]))
postconditions.description: Each output string is a permutation of the input string S (same multiset of characters).

postconditions.expression: all(is_lexicographically_smallest_partitionable(line, S, K) for line, S, K in zip(stdout_lines, [tc[1] for tc in test_cases_strings], [tc[1] for tc in test_cases]))
postconditions.description: Each output string is the lexicographically smallest string achievable by partitioning S into exactly K non-empty subsequences and concatenating them.
